_comment: RATCHET baseline for scripts/check-monitoring-schedules.mjs. Rows listed here violated CLAUDE.md's off-:00 boundary law at the moment the gate landed (OPS-MONITORING-SCHEDULE-SOT-W1, 2026-08-03): they REPORT, a NEW violation BLOCKS, and a baselined row moving to a DIFFERENT violating minute BLOCKS. This file only ever SHRINKS — deleting an entry is always allowed, adding one is a deliberate edit a reviewer sees.
_why_a_baseline: A fail-closed gate + known pre-existing violations + an explicit instruction not to fix them in that wave are mutually unsatisfiable: wired as a hard block, this gate would have failed every deploy from the commit that introduced it. Same resolution the repo already runs for scripts/check_test_baseline.sh vs audits/test-baseline-known-failures.txt.
_status: EMPTY — RETIRED. `entries` is zero-length, so this gate is now FULLY BLOCKING: any :00-boundary violation, pre-existing or new, fails. Kept as a file rather than deleted because an ABSENT baseline and an EMPTY one must stay distinguishable — the gate reads an unreadable/malformed baseline as INDETERMINATE, and deleting this would make 'nobody ever baselined anything' look identical to 'the debt was paid'.

retirement_record.why: Fired exactly ON the :00 boundary — the SEC-48 defect, on a load-bearing row. Tuesday 12:27 verified free against the LIVE crontab before the move: venue-slo-tiers-drift-canary holds 27 12 on MONDAY only, and the sole other Tuesday-noon job is daily-digest at 12:03.

A deliberate 15-minute grid whose trailing :58 sat 2 minutes before the next hour. ONLY the breaching member moved — :13/:28/:43 are already legal (offset 13/28/17) and were left alone rather than churned onto the canonical set for cosmetics, which is why this row still reports ADVISORY (:28 is off-set) rather than LEGAL. :57 was picked from a live minute census as the least-contended canonical minute on this host: no other HOURLY cron holds it, only two daily jobs (00:57 website-drift, 06:57 inventory-reconcile).
Same shape as webhook-delivery-canary — a 5-minute grid where only the trailing :58 breached; only that member moved. aoe-1 runs no other minute-grid cron, so there was nothing to collide with.

_safe_window_note: CLAUDE.md's cron safe-window rule ('next safe window >= 4h continuous; HALT if <=30min before a fire or <=2h after') is UNSATISFIABLE for a sub-hourly grid — a 5-minute cron never has a 4-hour gap — and it is written for a DESTRUCTIVE touch, which a crontab line edit is not: cron re-reads the file and an already-running job is unaffected. The real hazard when moving a minute is narrow: installing between the NEW (earlier) minute and the OLD one skips one fire. Both :58 -> :57 moves were installed at :33, 23 minutes clear of the :56-:58 danger window, with the box's own `date -u` read immediately before each install rather than inferred from session wall-clock.
